title: Rethinking Synthetic Rationale Supervision for Disease Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2606.10279v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning with synthetic rationales is widely assumed to improve clinical prediction by teaching models not only what to predict but why. We test this assumption on five-year Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) prediction from longitudinal health histories. In this setting, we generate training rationales using the correct labels, then fine-tune models to output a rationale followed by a label. Across a large-scale controlled experiment of 504 configurations, we find that Rationale First SFT consistently and substantially hurts predictive performance relative to Label Only fine-tuning. The degradation persists across model families and data scales, and is not resolved by using a reasoning-oriented base model. translated_title: 重新思考疾病预测中的合成推理监督
translated_abstract: 在监督微调中使用合成推理理由被广泛认为能够提升临床预测效果，因为它不仅教会模型“预测什么”，还教会模型“为什么这样预测”。我们在基于纵向健康病史的五年阿尔茨海默病及相关痴呆预测任务中检验了这一假设。在该设置中，我们使用正确标签生成训练推理理由，然后微调模型使其先输出推理理由、再输出标签。在一项涵盖504种配置的大规模对照实验中，我们发现“推理优先”的监督微调相比“仅标签”微调，始终且显著地损害了预测性能。这种性能退化在不同模型系列和数据规模上均持续存在，且使用面向推理的基础模型也无法解决。在一项采用固定协议的心血管疾病验证实验中重现了类似的发现。至关重要的是，这一失败并非由推理理由质量不佳所解释：人类专家标注证实了生成……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究发现，在疾病预测中使用合成推理理由进行“推理优先”监督微调反而会持续且显著地损害预测性能，且这种退化跨模型系列、数据规模和任务普遍存在，并非由推理理由质量不佳所致。
en_tdlr: Rationale-first supervised fine-tuning with synthetic rationales consistently and substantially hurts disease prediction performance compared to label-only fine-tuning, a degradation that persists across model families, data scales, and tasks, and is not explained by poor rationale quality.
